Subject: Finova - Post-call: Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific perf / SLO items we agreed to clarify:

1) Latency targets (p90 / p99) by region
   - US (primary): p90 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms (interactive UI flows)
   - EU: p90 <= 180ms, p99 <= 400ms
   - APAC: p90 <= 220ms, p99 <= 500ms

2) Throughput and concurrency
   - Steady-state throughput: ~120 qps (text-gen)
   - Burst capacity: up to 300 qps sustained for up to 10 minutes during peak windows
   - Typical concurrent sessions (user-facing streaming): 800 concurrent connections (mostly short-lived)

3) Streaming requirements
   - Need server-sent streaming for tokens-as-they-generate for chat UI. Client expects initial token within 200ms of request start for small prompts.

4) Data residency / routing constraints
   - EU customer PII must stay in EU region (APAC similar for specific customers). Routing must be region-aware with the ability to pin accounts to a region.

5) Fallbacks / SLA behavior
   - If regional capacity is constrained, acceptable fallback: route to nearest-region variant; must preserve data residency constraints for EU-locked customers (i.e., no cross-border routing for EU-locked).

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- We (Redwood) to validate feasibility of the latency targets against the selected model family and quantify expected cost impact per 1M tokens. (Aditya / Dev taking lead)
- Finova to share sample traffic profile (hourly qps, percent streaming vs non-streaming) and a short list of demo endpoints to simulate (you mentioned search-assisted compose + chat).
- Schedule an SE deep-dive to go through model variant choices, batching, and regional placement. Suggested slots: Mon/Tue next week.

Attachments: I attached the SLO requirements template we discussed and a lightweight spreadsheet area for you to drop traffic profile numbers (finova_slo_requirements.xlsx).

If any of the bullets above are incorrect or missing detail, call it out and I'll update. Otherwise we'll aim to have a feasibility note and cost delta by EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches my notes. Two clarifications from our side:

1) Latency targets: the p99 numbers you listed look reasonable for UI flows. For some regulatory reporting flows we can tolerate higher p99s, but the UI chat and search-assisted compose must hit the targets you listed.

2) Data residency: EU-locked customers cannot leave the EU for processing or storage. For APAC customers we're flexible but would prefer region-local if possible. We have a small set (~12%) of EU customers that must be pinned.

Action items from Finova:
- I attached a quick export of our hourly qps and user session durations (see attached CSV in the zip).
- We can make Mon 30th at 10am PT for the SE deep-dive — Priya will join as our infra lead.

One question: on fallback behavior, can Redwood guarantee that if EU capacity is saturated we will never have requests cross to US for EU-locked accounts? If that's a hard no, we need to know what the fallback looks like (queue, degraded model within EU, or reject).

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Finova - Post-call: Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (US/EU/APAC)

Appreciate the export, Alex — that helps a lot. Quick responses inline to your question and next steps: 

- EU-only routing for pinned customers: Yes — we can absolutely support region-pinning so that EU-locked accounts never leave EU infrastructure. That's a supported config for Private and Dedicated customers; for Hosted we provide a regional tenancy model with strong routing policies and can sign the contractual data residency clause. Fallbacks we can offer:
  * Local degraded model: keep traffic in EU but route to a smaller/quantized model variant hosted in the EU (we can guarantee no cross-border for pinned accounts).
  * Queue with backpressure: reject or queue incoming requests when EU capacity is fully saturated (policy-based).
  * Emergency cross-border only with explicit opt-in and additional legal sign-off (not default).

- Regarding guarantees: we can expose routing SLOs and capacity reservations as part of a Dedicated capacity contract. For Hosted customers, we can set routing policies and recommend Dedicated pools if strict hard guarantees are required.

Aditya / Dev will take the traffic CSV and run a short simulation (batching, KV cache hit assumptions, streaming overhead) and return:
  1) Expected p90/p99 per region with the proposed model family (and an alternative quantized option)
  2) Cost estimate delta per 1M tokens
  3) Suggested Dedicated pool sizing and suggested autoscale thresholds to meet the burst requirements

SE deep-dive: Mon 30 Mar, 10:00am PT works — I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda: model variants, batching/streaming tradeoffs, regional placement, and a proposed mutual action plan.

Next step for you: please confirm the attendee list (Priya + anyone from infra) and if you want us to include legal/ops for a short residency contract discussion.

Best,
Marissa
